Natural Conversations with Classmates
Scene 1: Before the First Class
You:
Hey, is this seat taken?
Camille:
No, go ahead.
You:
Thanks. Is this the room for the stochastic-processes class?
Camille:
I hope so. Otherwise, we’re both in the wrong place.
You:
That would be a strong start to the semester.
Camille:
Exactly. I’m Camille, by the way.
You:
Nice to meet you. I’m Alex.
Camille:
Nice to meet you too. Are you in the El Karoui program?
You:
Yes. I just moved to Paris a few days ago, so I’m still figuring everything out.
Camille:
Where did you move from?
You:
I’m from China. I studied mathematics there, and now I’m trying to get more exposure to quantitative
finance.
Camille:
That’s cool. How are you finding Paris so far?
You:
Honestly, I’ve barely had time to explore. Most of my time has gone into paperwork, finding my way
around, and trying not to get lost on the Métro.
Camille:
That sounds about right for the first week.

初次见面高频句型
• Is this seat taken?
• Do you mind if I sit here?
• Is this the room for…?
• Are you here for the same class?
• I’m [name], by the way.
• What program are you in?
• What did you study before this?
• Where did you move from?
• Have you been in Paris long?
• How are you finding Paris so far?
• Are you settling in okay?
How are you finding Paris?
意思不是“你怎么找到巴黎”，而是：
你觉得巴黎怎么样？
可替换：
• How are you finding the program?
• How are you finding the workload?
• How are you finding the class so far?
• How are you finding life in France?
回答：
• I’m enjoying it so far.
• It’s been good, although the first week was a bit overwhelming.
• I’m still getting used to it.
• It’s definitely different from what I expected.
• I haven’t formed a strong opinion yet.
• So far, so good.
I’m still figuring everything out.
我还在逐渐搞清楚所有事情。
非常高频，可用于新学校、新城市、新工作：
• I’m still figuring out the transport system.
• I’m still figuring out how the exams work.
• I’m still figuring out what roles I want to apply for.
Scene 2: Talking About Language
Camille:
Do you speak French?

You:
Only a little. I started learning recently, so I can handle very basic situations, but I’m much more
comfortable in English.
Camille:
Don’t worry. A lot of people in the program speak English.
You:
That’s reassuring. I’m trying to learn enough French for everyday life, but for technical discussions,
I’ll probably rely on English for a while.
Camille:
That makes sense. Just ask if you miss anything.
You:
Thanks, I appreciate it. And please feel free to correct me if I say something unnatural in English.
自然谈论语言能力
避免直接说：
My English is very poor.
My French is zero.
更自然：
• I’m still learning French.
• My French is quite basic at the moment.
• I can handle simple situations, but I’m not conversational yet.
• I can usually follow the main idea, although I may miss some details.
• I’m much more comfortable in English.
• I may need you to repeat things occasionally.
• I understand more than I can express.
• I know the technical term, but I’m not sure how to pronounce it.
• I’m still getting used to different accents.
听不清时：
• Sorry, I didn’t catch the last part.
• Could you say that again?
• What was the word you used after “variance”?
• Could you speak a little more slowly?
• I caught the general idea, but I missed the details.
• Sorry, I’m not familiar with that expression.
• What does that mean in this context?
• Do you mean that…?
I didn’t catch that.
比“I didn’t hear you”更常用。它通常表示没听清，不是质疑对方没有说话。

Scene 3: During the Break
Adam:
Are you two going downstairs for coffee?
Camille:
Yes. Do you want to come?
You:
Sure, I’m in.
Adam:
I’m Adam, by the way. I don’t think we’ve met.
You:
I’m Alex. Nice to meet you.
Adam:
Likewise. What’s your background?
You:
Mostly mathematics and probability. I’ve done some programming, but I’m trying to become much
stronger at writing clean, reliable code.
What about you?
Adam:
I studied engineering. I worked for a year before joining the program.
You:
What kind of work were you doing?
Adam:
Mostly data analysis and risk modeling. It was interesting, but I wanted something more mathematically
challenging.
You:
That makes sense. Are you aiming for research roles?
Adam:
Probably, although I’m keeping an open mind. I’m also interested in trading.
You:
Same here. I’m leaning more toward research at the moment, but I haven’t ruled anything out.
加入活动
• Are you going downstairs?
• Are you guys getting coffee?

• Do you want to come?
• Mind if I join you?
• Is it okay if I tag along?
• Sure, I’m in.
• Yeah, I’m down.
• I’d be up for that.
• Sounds good.
• Why not?
语气差异：
I’m in.
自然、常用：算我一个。
I’m down.
更随意：我愿意、我参加。适合同学，不适合正式面试。
I’d be up for that.
我愿意参加。
Mind if I join you?
介意我加入吗？自然且不过度客气。
tag along
跟着一起去，较随意：
Mind if I tag along?
Scene 4: Discussing Career Plans
Camille:
Have you started applying for internships yet?
You:
Not seriously. I’ve been looking at different firms and trying to understand the recruiting timelines, but
I’m still building up my interview preparation.
Adam:
What are you focusing on?
You:
Probability, statistics, algorithms, and mental math. I’m also practicing how to explain my reasoning
out loud. I often know how to solve a problem on paper, but explaining it clearly in real time is a different
skill.
Adam:
Definitely. I had the same issue last year.

You:
How did you work on it?
Adam:
Mostly mock interviews. I also recorded myself solving problems and listened back to identify where my
explanations became unclear.
You:
That’s exactly what I’ve started doing. It feels awkward, but I can see why it helps.
Camille:
We could organize a small mock-interview group.
You:
I’d be very interested in that. It would be useful to practice with people who are preparing for similar
roles.
Adam:
Let’s create a group chat.
谈求职的自然问题
• Have you started applying yet?
• What kinds of roles are you targeting?
• Are you leaning toward research or trading?
• Are you applying mainly in London or Paris?
• How are you preparing for interviews?
• Which topics are you focusing on?
• Have you done any mock interviews?
• Do you know when recruiting starts?
• Have you heard back from anyone?
• How did the first round go?
• What was the interview like?
• Was it mostly technical or behavioral?
• Did they ask probability questions?
• How long did the process take?
• Are you keeping your options open?
I’m leaning toward research.
目前比较倾向研究，但还没有完全决定。
• I’m leaning toward quant research.
• I’m leaning more toward systematic trading.
• I’m leaning toward London, although Paris is still an option.
• I haven’t ruled anything out yet.
I’m keeping an open mind.
我保持开放，不急于排除其他可能性。
I haven’t ruled it out.
我还没有排除它。

Scene 5: Asking About Classes and Exams
You:
By the way, do people usually attend all the lectures?
Camille:
It depends on the course. Some lectures are useful, but people often prioritize the problem sets and past
exams.
You:
That’s what I’ve heard. Do students usually study alone or in groups?
Adam:
A bit of both. People often work independently at first and then compare solutions.
You:
Would you be up for comparing answers sometime? I sometimes spend too long on one approach
without realizing there’s a simpler one.
Camille:
Sure. We’re planning to work on the first problem set this weekend.
You:
Great. Keep me posted.
询问学校“潜规则”
• Do people usually attend this class?
• Is attendance required?
• How important are the lectures for the exam?
• Is the exam mainly based on the problem sets?
• Are past papers available?
• How difficult is the grading?
• Do people usually work in groups?
• Is the workload manageable?
• Which courses tend to be the hardest?
• Is the professor approachable?
• Does the professor provide solutions?
• How early do people start preparing for the exam?
• Is there anything you wish you had known at the beginning?
提议一起学习
• Would you be up for studying together?
• Do you want to compare solutions later?
• We could go through the problem set together.
• Let me know if you want to practice interviews.
• Feel free to send me your solution.
• I can share my notes with you.

• We should set up a study group.
• Keep me posted.
• Let me know what you decide.
Would you be up for…?
自然、友好，不会给对方太大压力。
Would you be up for doing a mock interview this weekend?
更直接：
Do you want to do a mock interview this weekend?
降低压力：
No pressure, but let me know if you’d be interested.
Scene 6: Lunch Conversation
Adam:
Are you guys heading to lunch?
Camille:
Yes. We were thinking of grabbing something nearby.
You:
Do you have anywhere in mind?
Camille:
There’s a small place around the corner. It’s quick and not too expensive.
You:
Sounds perfect.
Adam:
How are you finding the food in Paris?
You:
I like it, but I haven’t tried much yet. I’ve mostly been eating whatever is easy while I deal with
administrative stuff.
Camille:
Any food you don’t eat?
You:
No major restrictions. I’m not a huge fan of very sweet food, but otherwise I’m fairly easygoing.

Adam:
Have you tried any French dishes yet?
You:
A few, although I’m terrible at remembering the names. You may have to educate me.
Camille:
We’ll give you a list.
吃饭场景
• Are you heading to lunch?
• Do you want to grab lunch?
• We’re grabbing a quick bite.
• Do you have anywhere in mind?
• I’m fine with anything.
• I’m not too picky.
• I have no major dietary restrictions.
• I’m vegetarian.
• I’m allergic to…
• I’m not a huge fan of…
• I could go for something warm.
• Shall we split the bill?
• I’ll get this one.
• You can get the next one.
grab lunch / grab a coffee / grab a bite
非常高频，意思是去简单吃饭或喝咖啡，不表示真的“抓”。
I’m fairly easygoing.
这里表示对选择不太挑剔。
I could go for…
我现在挺想要……
• I could go for a coffee.
• I could go for something spicy.
• I could go for an early night.
Scene 7: Moving Beyond Small Talk
Camille:
What do you usually do outside of studying?
You:
I’ve been so focused on preparing for the program that I haven’t done much recently. But I enjoy
running, watching films, and exploring new places when I have time.
How about you?

Camille:
I’m into climbing. I go a couple of times a week.
You:
I’ve never tried it, but I’d be curious to give it a go.
Camille:
You should come sometime. The place I go to is beginner-friendly.
You:
I might take you up on that.
Adam:
I mostly play football and spend too much time watching it.
You:
Which team do you support?
Adam:
Paris Saint-Germain, unfortunately.
You:
Why unfortunately?
Adam:
Because supporting them is emotionally exhausting.
You:
Fair enough.
兴趣聊天
• What do you do outside of studying?
• What are you into?
• What do you do for fun?
• Have you been watching anything good lately?
• What kind of music are you into?
• Do you play any sports?
• Have you explored much of Paris?
• Is there anywhere you’d recommend?
• How did you get into that?
• How often do you go?
• I’ve never tried it.
• I’ve been meaning to try that.
• I’d be curious to give it a go.
• I might take you up on that.

I’ve been meaning to…
我一直想做，但还没有真正开始。
• I’ve been meaning to visit that museum.
• I’ve been meaning to start running again.
• I’ve been meaning to ask you about the exam.
I might take you up on that.
我可能真的会接受你的提议。
例如别人说：
You can borrow my notes.
你可以回答：
Thanks. I might take you up on that.
Scene 8: Not Understanding a Joke or Reference
Adam:
The professor’s explanation was basically the mathematical version of “trust me, bro.”
You:
Sorry, I know what “trust me” means, but I’m not familiar with that expression.
Adam:
It’s an internet joke. It means someone is making a claim without providing evidence.
You:
Got it. So you mean he stated the result without really proving it.
Adam:
Exactly.
You:
That makes sense. I’ll probably miss quite a few cultural references at first, so feel free to explain them.
不懂梗时不必假装
• I’m not familiar with that reference.
• Is that from a film?
• Is that an expression?
• What does that mean?
• I know the words, but I don’t understand the joke.
• Is that sarcastic?
• Are you joking, or are you serious?
• Got it.
• That makes sense now.

• So, basically, you mean…?
trust me, bro
网络化、调侃性表达，指一个人提出结论但不给可靠证据。只适合非正式聊天。
不要急着大量学习网络俚语。更重要的是掌握：
I’m not familiar with that reference. What does it mean?
Scene 9: Making Plans
Camille:
A few of us are going for drinks on Friday. Would you like to join?
You:
Yes, I’d be up for that. What time are you thinking?
Camille:
Probably around seven, but we haven’t finalized anything.
You:
Seven should work for me. Just send me the details when you know.
Adam:
We may go somewhere near the Latin Quarter.
You:
Sounds good. I’m still learning my way around, so I may need very specific directions.
Camille:
No problem. We’ll send you the location.
约时间
• Would you like to join?
• Are you free on Friday?
• Do you have plans this weekend?
• We’re thinking of going to…
• What time are you thinking?
• Seven works for me.
• I’m flexible.
• I should be free after six.
• I’ll confirm later today.
• Just send me the details.
• Let’s lock in a time.
• We can play it by ear.
• I may be a few minutes late.
• I’m running about ten minutes late.
• Something came up.

• Could we push it back to eight?
• Can I take a rain check?
Let’s lock in a time.
让我们把时间确定下来。
play it by ear
先不完全决定，根据情况临时安排。
We don’t need a detailed plan. Let’s play it by ear.
take a rain check
这次不能参加，希望以后再约：
I can’t make it tonight. Could I take a rain check?
Scene 10: Group-Chat Messages
加入群聊
Camille:
I’ve added you to the class group chat.
You:
Thanks. I appreciate it. I’ll try not to ask too many questions on the first day.
Camille:
Ask as many as you need. That’s what the group is for.
确认计划
Adam:
Are we still on for the mock interview at 3 p.m.?
You:
Yes, 3 p.m. works for me. Shall we meet in the library?
Adam:
Perfect. I’ll book a room.
迟到
You:
I’m running about ten minutes late. Sorry about that.
Adam:
No worries. Take your time.

You:
Thanks. I’m on my way now.
改期
You:
Something unexpected came up this afternoon. Would it be possible to move our session to tomorrow?
Adam:
Tomorrow works. Same time?
You:
Yes, that would be perfect. Thanks for being flexible.
发资料
You:
I’ve uploaded my solution to the shared folder. I’m not fully confident about the final step, so please
let me know if you spot an issue.
Camille:
Thanks. I’ll take a look tonight.
结束聊天
You:
Thanks for today. The discussion was really helpful.
Camille:
Same here. We should do it again next week.
You:
Definitely. Keep me posted about the next problem set.
自然口语中最值得掌握的回应
表示同意
• Exactly.
• Definitely.
• Absolutely.
• That makes sense.
• That’s true.
• Good point.

• Fair point.
• I agree.
• Same here.
• That’s how I see it as well.
部分同意
• To some extent.
• I see what you mean.
• I get where you’re coming from.
• That’s true, although…
• I agree with the general point, but…
• It depends.
• I’m not sure it’s always the case.
表示惊讶或兴趣
• Really?
• No way.
• That’s interesting.
• That’s good to know.
• I hadn’t thought of that.
• How did that happen?
• What was that like?
• Tell me more.
• That sounds intense.
• That sounds like a lot.
表示理解
• Got it.
• I see.
• That makes sense.
• Right, I’m with you.
• Okay, that clears it up.
• I see what you mean now.
表示没问题
• No problem.
• No worries.
• It’s all good.
• That’s fine.
• Don’t worry about it.
• Take your time.
自然结束一段对话
• Anyway, I should probably get going.
• I’ll let you get back to work.

• It was nice talking to you.
• I’ll see you in class.
• Catch you later.
• Speak soon.
• Keep me posted.
• We should do this again sometime.
对话延续公式
许多英语学习者能够回答问题，但不会把问题抛回去。使用下面的公式：
回答 + 补充一点信息 + 反问对方
例如：
Question:
What did you study before this?
Weak answer:
Mathematics.
Natural answer:
I studied mathematics, mainly probability and statistics. I’m now trying to build a stronger foundation
in finance and programming. What about you?
另一个例子：
Question:
How are you finding Paris?
Natural answer:
I’m enjoying it so far, although the administrative side has been a little overwhelming. I haven’t
explored much yet. Have you lived here for long?
再例如：
Question:
Are you applying for trading roles?
Natural answer:
Possibly. I’m leaning more toward research at the moment, but I’m still keeping an open mind. What
kinds of roles are you targeting?
这套结构能显著减少聊天突然结束的情况。

Discussing a Monte Carlo Assignment
Scene
Three students—Alex, Léa, and Daniel—are discussing a problem set on Monte Carlo methods.
The assignment asks them to compare a standard Monte Carlo estimator with an antithetic-variables
estimator for the price of a European option.
Part 1: Starting the Discussion
Alex:
Did either of you get anywhere with Question Four?
Léa:
I have a partial solution, but I’m not completely confident about the variance comparison.
Daniel:
Same here. I understand why both estimators are unbiased, but I don’t think we can simply claim that
the antithetic estimator always has lower variance.
Alex:
That was my concern as well. Léa, could you walk us through your setup?
Léa:
Sure. Let Z be a standard normal random variable. We generate one path using Z and an antithetic path
using −Z. If the discounted payoffs are Y (Z) and Y (−Z), the paired estimator is
(Y(Z) + Y(−Z)) / 2.
Since Z and −Z have the same distribution, both payoff terms have the same expectation. Therefore,
their average has the same expectation as the original estimator.
Alex:
I’m with you so far.
高迁移句型：开始讨论
• Did you get anywhere with Question Four?
• How far did you get with the assignment?
• Have you made any progress on the proof?
• I have a partial solution.
• I got as far as the second part.
• I understand the setup, but I’m stuck on…
• I think I see the main idea, but the details are still unclear.
• I’m not completely confident about…

• Could you walk me through your approach?
• How did you set the problem up?
Did you get anywhere with…?
这里不是质疑对方能力，而是自然地问“你这部分做得怎么样了”。
更中性：
Have you made any progress on…?
更随意：
Any luck with Question Four?
Part 2: Asking for Clarification
Alex:
I follow the unbiasedness argument. What I don’t see is why the variance must be lower.
Léa:
My intuition was that the two payoffs should move in opposite directions because they are generated
using opposite shocks.
Daniel:
That sounds plausible, but I think we need to be more precise. Using opposite shocks does not
automatically guarantee that the payoffs are negatively correlated.
Léa:
You’re right. I phrased that too strongly.
Alex:
Could we write the variance explicitly? That might make the condition clearer.
Daniel:
Yes. Assuming the two terms have the same variance,
Var((Y(Z) + Y(−Z))/2) = ½ Var(Y(Z)) + ½ Cov(Y(Z), Y(−Z)).
So the variance is reduced when the covariance term is negative.
Alex:
Right. That makes the condition transparent.
高迁移句型：表示“我听懂了一部分”
• I follow the argument up to this point.
• I’m with you so far.
• That part makes sense.

• I understand how you obtained the first equation.
• I see the intuition.
• I agree with the general direction.
然后接具体疑问：
• What I don’t see is why…
• What I’m missing is the step from A to B.
• I’m not sure how the final equality follows.
• Could you clarify what you mean by…?
• Where are we using the independence assumption?
• Is this an equality or an approximation?
• Does this hold for every payoff function?
• Are we proving this theoretically or observing it numerically?
避免只说：
I don’t understand.
更有效的是：
I understand why the estimator is unbiased. What I don’t understand is why the
covariance must be negative.
Part 3: Disagreeing Politely
Léa:
For a call option, though, shouldn’t the covariance always be negative?
Daniel:
I think that is often true in the standard Black–Scholes setup because the payoff is monotone in the
underlying shock. But I’d be hesitant to state it without specifying the assumptions.
Alex:
Let me push back slightly. Even if the payoff is monotone, do we know that the transformed payoffs are
negatively correlated for every parameter choice?
Daniel:
That’s a fair question. We should probably distinguish between the general antithetic method and this
particular payoff under this particular model.
Léa:
Agreed. My original statement was too broad. A safer version would be: in this setting, the antithetic
construction is expected to produce negative covariance and therefore reduce variance.
Alex:
That sounds more defensible.

礼貌反对的层级
轻度保留
• I’m not sure that follows.
• I wonder if we’re assuming too much there.
• I’d be a little careful with that claim.
• I’m not fully convinced by the last step.
• I see the intuition, but I’m not sure the argument is complete.
• That may be true here, but perhaps not in general.
明确但礼貌地反对
• I see it differently.
• I don’t think that conclusion follows from the assumptions.
• I think we may be conflating two different issues.
• That argument only goes through if…
• I would disagree with the claim that…
• Let me push back slightly.
接住对方观点再修改
• I see where you’re coming from, but…
• That’s a reasonable intuition. The issue is…
• I agree with the first part. Where I differ is…
• Your conclusion may be right, but I think we need a different justification.
• I think we’re saying similar things, but using different assumptions.
Let me push back slightly
常见于专业讨论，意思是“让我稍微提出一点反对意见”。语气取决于声音，应平静而非攻击性。
Part 4: Separating Intuition from Proof
Daniel:
Maybe we should separate the intuitive explanation from the formal argument.
The intuitive explanation is that pairing a large positive shock with an equally large negative shock can
offset some of the variability.
The formal argument is that the variance of the paired average contains a covariance term. If that
covariance is negative, the total variance is lower than the variance obtained from two independent
observations.
Léa:
That distinction helps. We can present the intuition first and then state the exact condition.
Alex:
We should also be explicit about what we are holding fixed. Are we comparing estimators using the same
number of payoff evaluations?

Daniel:
Good point. Otherwise, the computational comparison would not be fair.
区分直觉与严格论证
• Intuitively,…
• At a high level,…
• Roughly speaking,…
• The basic idea is…
• More formally,…
• To make that precise,…
• The exact statement is…
• Strictly speaking,…
• This is only a heuristic.
• That gives us intuition, but not a proof.
• We need to distinguish between a sufficient condition and a necessary condition.
• We need to separate the mathematical claim from the empirical observation.
例如：
Intuitively, diversification reduces risk. More formally, the reduction depends on the
covariance structure.
The simulation suggests that the estimator performs better, but that is empirical evidence
rather than a general proof.
Part 5: Checking Assumptions
Alex:
Let’s list the assumptions before we write the solution.
First, Z is standard normal.
Second, the stock price is generated under the same risk-neutral model for both Z and −Z.
Third, the two payoff evaluations are paired.
Fourth, when we compare efficiency, we keep the total computational budget fixed.
Am I missing anything?
Léa:
We should probably mention that the discount factor is the same for both paths.
Daniel:
Also, if we claim variance reduction for the call payoff, we should specify the monotonicity argument or
avoid making the claim universal.

Alex:
Right. Let’s word it carefully.
检查假设的句型
• What assumptions are we making?
• Where exactly do we use independence?
• Does the argument rely on normality?
• Are we working under the physical measure or the risk-neutral measure?
• Are the parameters assumed to be constant?
• Are we ignoring transaction costs?
• Is the process Markovian?
• Are we conditioning on the current filtration?
• Does the result still hold if the observations are dependent?
• What breaks if this assumption is removed?
• Is this assumption essential, or is it only used for convenience?
“Am I missing anything?”
非常自然，可用于让其他人补充：
• Am I missing anything?
• Is there anything else we need to include?
• Does that cover all the assumptions?
• Have I overlooked a case?
• Is there a boundary condition we haven’t considered?
Part 6: Testing Edge Cases
Daniel:
Before we finalize the argument, let’s test a few limiting cases.
If the payoff were linear in Z, the antithetic average might remove the random component entirely.
Léa:
Right. And if the payoff were an even function of Z, then Y (Z) and Y (−Z) would be identical, so the
antithetic construction would provide no benefit.
Alex:
That’s a useful contrast. It shows that the effectiveness of the method depends on the structure of the
payoff.
Daniel:
Exactly. Edge cases help us see which part of the reasoning is doing the work.

Léa:
I also implemented both estimators. The antithetic version appears to have a narrower confidence

One hundred thousand paired samples.
Daniel:

Léa:
Not initially.
Daniel:
That could make the comparison noisier. It might be better to use common random numbers so that the

Alex:
Could the discrepancy also come from the way the standard error is calculated? With paired

Léa:
That’s a good catch. I calculated the standard error using all payoff values separately. I should

Daniel:
That may explain the result.

• Is the result stable across different seeds?
• What is the confidence interval?

Alex:
I think we may be talking past each other.
When I say “more efficient,” I mean lower variance for a fixed number of payoff evaluations.
Daniel, I think you mean lower computational time for a fixed target accuracy.
Daniel:
Yes, exactly. Those are related, but they are not identical.
Léa:

Alex:
Works for me.

Daniel:
How should we organize the final answer?

I suggest four parts.
First, define the standard and antithetic estimators.
Second, prove that the antithetic estimator is unbiased.
Third, derive the variance expression and explain the role of covariance.
Fourth, present the numerical results under a fixed computational budget.
Alex:
That structure makes sense. I’d also add a brief comment explaining that variance reduction is not

Daniel:
Agreed. That qualification is important.

Alex:
How about this: I’ll write the unbiasedness argument and the variance derivation.

Alex:
Before we stop, let me summarize where we landed.
Both estimators are unbiased.

The antithetic estimator has lower variance when the paired payoffs have sufficiently negative

For the European call in the standard setup, we expect variance reduction, but we will state the relevant

Agreed.

学术讨论万能框架
遇到任何专业问题，可以按照这个顺序表达：
1. 说明你理解了什么
I understand why [A].
2. 精确指出不理解的部分
What I don’t see is how we get from [A] to [B].
3. 检查假设

4. 给出暂定判断

5. 提出验证办法

6. 总结结论

完整示例：
I understand why the estimator is unbiased. What I don’t see is why its variance must
always be lower. Are we assuming that the paired payoffs are negatively correlated? My
current understanding is that variance reduction depends on that covariance term. Could
we verify this by writing the variance explicitly? So, subject to negative covariance, the
antithetic estimator is more efficient.

A Complete Quant Interview
Part 1: Opening and Small Talk
Interviewer:
Hi, thanks for joining us today. How are you doing?
Candidate:
I’m doing well, thank you. I’ve been looking forward to the conversation. How are you?
Interviewer:
I’m good, thanks. Did you have any trouble finding the office?
Candidate:
Not at all. I gave myself some extra time, so I arrived a little early.
Interviewer:
Great. Before we get into the technical questions, could you briefly introduce yourself?
Candidate:
Of course. I studied mathematics and statistics, with a particular focus on probability, stochastic
processes, and numerical methods. Over the past year, I’ve become increasingly interested in
quantitative finance because it combines rigorous mathematical thinking with practical decision-making
under uncertainty.
I’m currently preparing to begin the El Karoui master’s program in Paris. Alongside my coursework,
I’ve been working through probability problems, implementing numerical methods in Python, and
improving the way I communicate technical ideas in English.
What I’m looking for now is a role where I can solve challenging problems, learn from strong
researchers, and gradually develop a deeper understanding of how quantitative models behave in real
market settings.
高迁移句型
I studied [A], with a particular focus on [B].
我学习了A，尤其关注B。
可替换：
• I studied applied mathematics, with a particular focus on optimization and probability.
• I studied computer science, with a particular focus on algorithms and machine learning.
• I studied physics, with a particular focus on statistical mechanics and numerical simulation.
Over the past [period], I’ve become increasingly interested in [field] because…
过去一段时间，我对某领域越来越感兴趣，因为……

比下面这种表达更自然：
• My interest is quantitative finance.
• I like quant very much.
What I’m looking for now is a role where I can…
我现在希望寻找的是一个能够让我……的岗位。
这是一种很实用的总结结构：
What I’m looking for now is a role where I can contribute, learn, and grow.
Part 2: Why Quantitative Finance?
Interviewer:
What specifically attracts you to quantitative finance?
Candidate:
There are three things that appeal to me.
First, I enjoy problems where the answer is not immediately obvious and where you have to make your
assumptions explicit. Quantitative finance forces you to distinguish between what is mathematically true,
what is statistically supported, and what is practically useful.
Second, I like the feedback loop. You can formulate a model, test it on data, identify where it breaks
down, and refine it. I find that combination of theory and empirical validation very motivating.
Third, I enjoy working in environments where people challenge each other’s reasoning. I don’t mind
being told that an argument is incomplete, provided that the discussion helps us arrive at a better
answer.
I also want to be careful not to overstate my experience. I’m still early in my development, but I’ve
found that I genuinely enjoy the underlying work: probability, modeling, coding, and explaining why a
method should or should not work.
高迁移句型
There are three things that appeal to me.
有三个方面特别吸引我。
这是非常自然的结构化开场。也可以说：
• There are two main reasons.
• A few things stand out to me.
• What appeals to me most is the combination of A and B.
I want to be careful not to overstate my experience.
我不想夸大自己的经验。

这是面试里非常好用的“诚实但不自我贬低”表达。
可以继续接：
• I haven’t worked on this in a professional setting yet, but…
• My exposure has mainly been academic so far.
• I’m still building depth in this area.
• I wouldn’t claim to be an expert, but I have developed a solid foundation.
不要频繁说：
• I know nothing about this.
• My English is bad.
• I am not very experienced.
更好的说法是：
My experience is still limited, but I’ve been approaching the subject systematically.
Part 3: Beginning a Technical Question
Interviewer:
Let’s move on to a probability question.
You repeatedly roll a fair six-sided die. What is the expected number of rolls required to observe two
consecutive sixes?
Candidate:
Let me restate the problem to make sure I have it right.
We repeatedly roll a fair six-sided die, and we stop as soon as we observe a six immediately followed by
another six. We want the expected total number of rolls until that happens. Is that correct?
Interviewer:
Yes.
Candidate:
Great. Are the rolls independent?
Interviewer:
Yes, they are independent.
Candidate:
Okay. My first instinct might be to say thirty-six, because the probability of two sixes in a particular pair of
rolls is one over thirty-six. But that argument is too quick because consecutive pairs overlap. For
example, rolls one and two form a pair, but rolls two and three also form a pair.
So I think the cleanest way to approach this is to define states based on how much progress we have
made toward the pattern.

高迁移句型：确认题目
Let me restate the problem to make sure I have it right.
其他自然版本：
• Let me make sure I understand the setup.
• Just to confirm, we are assuming that…
• So, if I understand correctly, we stop when…
• Before I start, can I clarify one detail?
• Are we allowed to assume that…?
• Does the order matter here?
• Are repeated values allowed?
• Should I give an exact answer or an approximation?
• Are we optimizing expected value, worst-case performance, or both?
面试中确认题目不是能力不足。相反，它表明你知道答案依赖于假设。
高迁移句型：提出初步想法但不仓促承诺
My first instinct is to…
可替换：
• My initial thought is to use conditioning.
• My first instinct is to look for symmetry.
• I’m leaning toward a dynamic-programming approach.
• A natural starting point would be to consider a simpler case.
• The first approach that comes to mind is simulation, although there may be a cleaner analytical
solution.
• I see two possible approaches.
• I’m not fully committed to this yet, but I’d start by…
“I'm leaning toward…”表示“目前更倾向于”，非常适合尚未完全确定时使用。
高迁移句型：发现直觉可能不严谨
• That argument is a little too quick.
• I want to be careful here.
• That reasoning ignores the dependence created by overlap.
• I don’t think I can treat these events as independent.
• Let me sanity-check that.
• There may be a subtle issue with that approach.
• I think that gives the right intuition, but not yet a complete argument.
sanity-check是技术工作中非常常见的口语，意思是做一个快速合理性检查。

Part 4: Thinking Aloud and Solving the Problem
Candidate:
Let E₀ be the expected number of additional rolls when the previous roll was not a six, or when we have
not rolled anything yet.
Let E₁ be the expected number of additional rolls given that the most recent roll was a six.
Starting from state zero, we always use one roll.
With probability five-sixths, the new roll is not a six, so we remain in state zero. With probability one-sixth,
we roll a six and move to state one.
Therefore,
E₀ = 1 + (5/6)E₀ + (1/6)E₁.
Starting from state one, we again use one roll.
With probability one-sixth, we roll another six and finish. With probability five-sixths, we roll something
other than six and return to state zero.
Therefore,
E₁ = 1 + (5/6)E₀.
From the first equation,
E₀ = 6 + E₁.
Substituting the second equation gives
E₀ = 6 + 1 + (5/6)E₀.
So,
(1/6)E₀ = 7,
which means
E₀ = 42.
Therefore, the expected number of rolls is forty-two.
Interviewer:
Why is it larger than thirty-six?
Candidate:
Because a failed attempt does not always reset us after exactly two rolls, and the candidate pairs overlap.

More importantly, rolling one six creates partial progress, but if the next roll is not a six, that progress is
lost.
The value thirty-six would be a tempting estimate if we treated every non-overlapping pair as an
independent trial. That would actually give an expected number of seventy-two rolls, since each trial
would consist of two rolls. But that procedure would waste information by ignoring overlapping pairs.
The state-based method accounts for the fact that a single six puts us closer to completion.
Interviewer:
That’s right.
高迁移句型：解释推导
• Let me define two states.
• I’m conditioning on the outcome of the next roll.
• There are two cases to consider.
• In the first case, we remain in the same state.
• In the second case, we move to…
• This gives us the following recursion.
• Substituting the second equation into the first, we obtain…
• After simplifying, we get…
• The result follows directly from…
• The key observation is that…
• The intuition is that…
说公式时的完整表达
不要只说：
E zero equals one plus five over six E zero.
最好说：
Starting from state zero, we first spend one roll. With probability five-sixths, we return to
the same state, and with probability one-sixth, we move to state one.
先解释含义，再读公式。
回答“为什么”的结构
The result is larger than [benchmark] because [mechanism].
Another way to see this is that [alternative intuition].
例如：
• The variance is lower because the two estimators are negatively correlated.
• The estimator is biased because the nonlinear transformation does not commute with
expectation.
• The algorithm is slow because the same quantity is recomputed at every iteration.

• The strategy fails because it relies on information that is not available at decision time.
Part 5: Correcting Yourself Gracefully
Interviewer:
Suppose the die is biased and the probability of rolling a six is p. How would the answer change?
Candidate:
My initial guess would be 1/p², but let me check that rather than committing to it.
Using the same state definitions,
E₀ = 1 + (1 − p)E₀ + pE₁
and
E₁ = 1 + (1 − p)E₀.
From the first equation,
pE₀ = 1 + pE₁,
so
E₀ = 1/p + E₁.
Substituting the second equation,
E₀ = 1/p + 1 + (1 − p)E₀.
Therefore,
pE₀ = 1/p + 1,
and hence
E₀ = (1 + p)/p².
So my initial guess of 1/p² was missing an additional 1/p term.
Interviewer:
Exactly.
Candidate:
That makes sense. The additional term reflects the expected cost of repeatedly losing the partial progress
created by the first success.

高迁移句型：改正错误
面试中算错并不可怕，掩饰或混乱才可怕。
• I think I made an incorrect assumption there.
• Let me correct that.
• I was treating those events as independent, which they are not.
• I’ve just noticed an issue with my previous step.
• Let me backtrack for a moment.
• The conclusion may still be correct, but my justification was incomplete.
• I need to revise the second equation.
• My initial guess was missing an additional term.
• Thanks—that points out exactly where my reasoning went off track.
不要反复说：
• Sorry, sorry, sorry.
• I’m terrible at this.
• I have no idea what I’m doing.
一次简短承认，立即回到推理：
You’re right. I overlooked the overlap. Let me revise the state transition.
Part 6: Handling a Hint
Interviewer:
Here is another question. Suppose X and Y are independent standard normal random variables. What is
the distribution of X + Y ?
Candidate:
Since they are independent Gaussian random variables, their sum is also Gaussian. The mean is zero, and
the variance is the sum of the individual variances, so the variance is two. Therefore,
X + Y ∼ N(0,2).
Interviewer:
Good. Now what about X + Y , conditional on X − Y ?
Candidate:
Let me think about the covariance structure.
We have
Cov(X + Y ,X − Y ) = Var(X) − Var(Y ) = 0.
Because the pair is jointly Gaussian, zero covariance implies independence. Therefore, conditioning on
X − Y does not change the distribution of X + Y , so it remains N(0,2).

Interviewer:
Exactly. What was the crucial property?
Candidate:
The crucial property was joint Gaussianity. In general, zero covariance would not be enough to conclude
independence.
高迁移句型：收到提示后继续
• Let me use that hint.
• That suggests looking at the covariance.
• I see where you’re going with that.
• Right, that reduces the problem to…
• That’s helpful. I was trying to solve a more general problem than necessary.
• Given that observation, the rest follows fairly directly.
• The missing ingredient is…
• The crucial assumption is…
• This would not hold in general because…

Part 7: Behavioral Question
Interviewer:
Tell me about a time when you encountered a difficult technical problem.
Candidate:
Certainly.
In a university project, my team was asked to price a path-dependent option using Monte Carlo
simulation and compare several variance-reduction methods.
My main responsibility was to implement the baseline estimator and make sure that the comparison
between methods was meaningful.
At first, different team members obtained noticeably different results, even though our code appeared to
implement the same model. Rather than immediately assuming that one person’s code was wrong, I
suggested that we establish a shared benchmark.
I created a minimal test case with fixed parameters and a fixed random seed. We then compared the
simulation path by path. That allowed us to identify two separate issues: one implementation used a
different discounting convention, and another calculated the payoff at the wrong time index.
After correcting those issues, I added unit tests for the payoff function, checked the estimator against a
case with a known analytical solution, and documented the assumptions we were using.
As a result, we obtained consistent estimates across implementations and could make a fair comparison
between the baseline, antithetic, and control-variate methods.

The main lesson for me was that when numerical results disagree, it is often more effective to reduce the
problem to a controlled benchmark than to inspect a large codebase line by line.

Situation：发生了什么？
In a university project, my team was asked to…
Task：你的责任是什么？
My main responsibility was to…

行为题高频追问
Interviewer:
What would you do differently now?
Candidate:
I would define the testing framework at the beginning of the project rather than waiting until the outputs
disagreed. We eventually solved the problem, but an agreed benchmark and a small set of unit tests
would have saved us time.
Interviewer:
Did you have any disagreements with your teammates?
Candidate:
Yes, although the disagreement was mainly about process rather than the final objective. One teammate
wanted to continue improving the model immediately, while I thought we first needed to verify the
baseline implementation.
I explained that adding complexity before establishing a reliable benchmark would make future
discrepancies harder to diagnose. We agreed to spend a limited amount of time validating the baseline
and then return to model improvements.

Interviewer:
What was your individual contribution?
Candidate:
The project was collaborative, so I don’t want to take credit for the entire result. My specific
contribution was designing the benchmark, identifying the inconsistent assumptions, and implementing
the validation tests.
避免含糊的团队回答
不要只说：
We did this. We solved that. We improved the model.
面试官会追问：你到底做了什么？

• My specific contribution was…
• I personally took ownership of…
• I was primarily responsible for…
• The decision was made as a team, but I led…
• One thing I initiated was…
Part 8: Not Knowing the Answer
Interviewer:
Are you familiar with rough volatility models?
Candidate:
I’m familiar with the motivation at a high level, particularly the idea that volatility may exhibit rougher
behavior than standard diffusion models imply. However, I haven’t studied the theory deeply enough to
give you a precise technical account.
My current understanding is that fractional or Volterra-type structures are used to capture this behavior,
but I would want to verify the exact formulation before saying more.
Interviewer:
That’s fine.

I don’t remember the exact coefficient off the top of my head, but I can derive it.

Do you have any questions for me?

Second, when junior researchers join the team, what usually distinguishes the people who progress

Those are good questions.

第一篇：礼貌、求助与听不懂时的自救法语
一、最重要的法国式礼貌结构
在法国，向陌生人、店员、司机、工作人员提问时，最稳妥的顺序是：
Bonjour + Excusez-moi + 请求 + s’il vous plaît + merci
例如：
Bonjour, excusez-moi, vous pourriez m’aider, s’il vous plaît ?
您好，不好意思，您可以帮我一下吗？
不要直接走过去说：
Où est la gare ?
火车站在哪里？
语法没有错，但容易显得突然。更自然的是：
Bonjour, excusez-moi, vous savez où se trouve la gare, s’il vous plaît ?
您好，不好意思，请问您知道火车站在哪里吗？
场景一：在街上问路
Vous：
Bonjour, excusez-moi de vous déranger. Je cherche la station de métro la plus proche.
您好，不好意思打扰您。我在找最近的地铁站。
Passant：
La station est à environ cinq minutes à pied. Vous continuez tout droit, puis vous tournez à gauche au
deuxième feu.
地铁站步行大约五分钟。您一直往前走，然后在第二个红绿灯左转。
Vous：
D’accord. Je continue tout droit et je tourne à gauche au deuxième feu, c’est bien ça ?
好的。我一直往前走，然后在第二个红绿灯左转，是这样吗？
Passant：
Oui, exactement. Vous verrez l’entrée du métro juste après la pharmacie.
对。经过药店以后，您就会看到地铁入口。

Vous：
Très bien, merci beaucoup pour votre aide.
好的，非常感谢您的帮助。
Passant：
Je vous en prie.
不客气。
可以替换的地点
Je cherche la station de métro la plus proche.
我在找最近的地铁站。
替换为：
• l’arrêt de bus：公交站
• la gare RER：RER车站
• la pharmacie：药店
• un distributeur de billets：自动取款机
• les toilettes：洗手间
• l’accueil：接待处
• le bâtiment principal：主楼
• la bibliothèque universitaire：大学图书馆
• le restaurant universitaire：大学食堂
• la salle 204：204教室
高频方向表达
• Continuez tout droit.
一直往前走。
• Tournez à droite / à gauche.
向右转／向左转。
• Traversez la rue.
穿过马路。
• C’est juste en face.
就在正对面。
• C’est à côté de la pharmacie.
在药店旁边。
• C’est entre la banque et la boulangerie.
在银行和面包店之间。
• C’est au bout de la rue.
在街道尽头。

• C’est à environ dix minutes à pied.
步行大约十分钟。
• Vous ne pouvez pas le rater.
您不会错过的／非常显眼。
没听懂方向时
Désolé, je n’ai pas bien compris. Vous pourriez me montrer sur Google Maps ?
不好意思，我没太听懂。您可以在Google Maps上给我指一下吗？
Vous pouvez me l’écrire, s’il vous plaît ?
您可以给我写下来吗？
Est-ce que je peux vous montrer l’adresse sur mon téléphone ?
我可以在手机上给您看地址吗？
场景二：听不懂对方说话
Employée：
Vous devez d’abord remplir ce formulaire, puis prendre rendez-vous en ligne.
您需要先填写这张表，然后在网上预约。
Vous：
Excusez-moi, je débute en français. Vous pourriez parler un peu plus lentement, s’il vous plaît ?
不好意思，我刚开始学法语。您可以说得稍微慢一点吗？
Employée：
Oui, bien sûr. D’abord, vous remplissez ce formulaire.
当然。首先，您填写这张表。
Vous：
D’accord. Et ensuite, je dois prendre rendez-vous sur Internet, c’est bien ça ?
好的。然后我要在网上预约，对吗？
Employée：
Oui. Le site est indiqué en bas de la page.
是的。网站写在页面下面。

Vous：
Je vois. Est-ce que vous pourriez entourer l’adresse du site pour moi ?
我明白了。您可以帮我把网站地址圈出来吗？
Employée：
Bien sûr.
当然可以。
Vous：
Merci beaucoup. C’est très gentil.
非常感谢。您真好。
六个最重要的听不懂自救句型
1. 请求重复
Vous pouvez répéter, s’il vous plaît ?
您可以重复一遍吗？
稍微更礼貌：
Vous pourriez répéter, s’il vous plaît ?
Vous pouvez... 已经礼貌； Vous pourriez... 更加柔和。
2. 请求说慢一点
Vous pouvez parler plus lentement, s’il vous plaît ?
您可以说慢一点吗？
不要说：
Parlez lentement.
这像命令。
3. 精确说明漏听了哪里
Je n’ai pas compris le dernier mot.
我没听懂最后一个词。

Je n’ai pas compris ce que je dois faire ensuite.
我没明白接下来应该做什么。
J’ai compris le début, mais pas la fin.
我听懂了开头，但没听懂后面。
比一句笼统的 Je ne comprends pas 更有效。
4. 请求换一种说法
Vous pouvez reformuler, s’il vous plaît ?
您可以换一种说法吗？
Vous pouvez l’expliquer plus simplement ?
您可以解释得简单一点吗？
5. 确认自己的理解
Si j’ai bien compris, je dois revenir demain matin.
如果我理解正确，我明天上午需要再来。
Donc, je dois envoyer le document par e-mail, c’est bien ça ?
所以我要通过电子邮件发送文件，对吗？
这个结构极其重要：
Donc, je dois [动作], c’est bien ça ?
可替换：
• payer ici：在这里付款
• attendre dehors：在外面等
• remplir ce formulaire：填写表格
• apporter mon passeport：带护照
• prendre rendez-vous：预约
• revenir lundi：星期一再来
6. 请求切换英语
最自然的顺序是：先尝试法语，再礼貌询问英语。
Excusez-moi, mon français est encore très limité. Est-ce que vous parlez anglais ?
不好意思，我的法语目前还很有限。您会说英语吗？

更简洁：
Est-ce qu’on peut parler anglais ?
我们可以说英语吗？
和工作人员说，优先用：
Est-ce que nous pouvons continuer en anglais ?
我们可以用英语继续吗？
场景三：向学校工作人员求助
Vous：
Bonjour Madame, excusez-moi de vous déranger. Je suis en M2 à Sorbonne Université et j’aurais besoin
d’un renseignement.
您好，女士，不好意思打扰您。我在索邦大学读M2，想咨询一个问题。
Employée：
Oui, je vous écoute.
好的，您说。
Vous：
Je voudrais savoir où je peux récupérer mon certificat de scolarité.
我想知道在哪里可以领取在读证明。
Employée：
Vous pouvez normalement le télécharger depuis votre espace étudiant.
通常您可以从学生个人页面下载。
Vous：
D’accord. Le problème, c’est que je n’arrive pas à me connecter à mon compte.
好的。问题是我无法登录账户。
Employée：
Vous avez déjà activé votre compte Sorbonne ?
您已经激活索邦账户了吗？
Vous：
Je ne suis pas sûr. Est-ce que vous pourriez me montrer la procédure ?

我不确定。您可以给我看一下流程吗？
Employée：
Oui. Vous devez aller sur cette page et cliquer ici.
可以。您要进入这个页面，然后点击这里。
Vous：
Très bien. Je vais essayer. Merci beaucoup pour votre aide.

Je voudrais savoir...
我想知道……
• Je voudrais savoir où je dois envoyer ce document.
• Je voudrais savoir si mon dossier est complet.
• Je voudrais savoir quand je recevrai ma carte étudiante.
• Je voudrais savoir comment prendre rendez-vous.
• Je voudrais savoir à qui je dois m’adresser.
J’aurais besoin de...
我需要……
• J’aurais besoin d’un renseignement.
• J’aurais besoin d’une attestation.
• J’aurais besoin d’aide pour remplir ce formulaire.
• J’aurais besoin de modifier mon adresse.
Je veux... 不是错误，但面对工作人员时， Je voudrais... 更自然。
场景四：自己不知道应该找谁
Vous：
Bonjour, excusez-moi. Je ne sais pas si je suis au bon endroit.
您好，不好意思。我不确定是不是应该来这里。
Employé：
Qu’est-ce que vous cherchez exactement ?
您具体需要办理什么？
Vous：
J’ai une question concernant mon inscription administrative.

我有一个关于行政注册的问题。

D’accord. Vous savez où se trouve le service de la scolarité ?

在二楼，112办公室。

Merci. Et est-ce qu’il faut prendre rendez-vous ?
谢谢。需要预约吗？
Employé：
Non, vous pouvez y aller directement.
不需要，您可以直接过去。

Je ne sais pas si je suis au bon endroit.
我不知道自己是不是来对地方了。
Je ne sais pas à qui m’adresser.
我不知道应该找谁。
Qui est-ce que je dois contacter ?
我应该联系谁？
Vous pourriez m’indiquer le bon service ?
您可以告诉我应该找哪个部门吗？

Vous：
Bonjour, je vous appelle au sujet de mon dossier étudiant.
您好，我打电话是想咨询我的学生材料。

Employée：
Oui, quel est le problème ?
好的，是什么问题？

J’ai envoyé les documents la semaine dernière, mais mon dossier apparaît toujours comme incomplet.
我上周已经提交了文件，但系统仍然显示我的材料不完整。

Vous：

电话中听不懂
Excusez-moi, la ligne n’est pas très bonne. Vous pouvez répéter ?
不好意思，信号不太好。您可以重复一下吗？

Vous pouvez me l’envoyer par e-mail ?

“tu”和“vous”怎么选
使用 vous
用于：
• 陌生人

• 刚认识且关系不明确的人
使用 tu
用于：
• 同学
• 朋友
• 年轻人之间
• 对方主动对你使用 tu
• 对方说： On peut se tutoyer.
On peut se tutoyer ?
我们可以互相用“tu”吗？
同学之间通常很快就使用 tu 。
高频礼貌回应
• Merci beaucoup.
非常感谢。
• Merci pour votre aide.
谢谢您的帮助。
• C’est très gentil.
您真好。

不客气，较正式。

不客气。
• Pas de problème.
没问题。
• Pas de souci.
没事、没问题，日常非常常见。
• Avec plaisir.
乐意效劳。
• Bonne journée.

• Bonne soirée.

进入商店时说 Bonjour ，离开时说：
Merci, au revoir. Bonne journée.

第三篇：和法国同学自然交流
同学之间通常使用 tu 。以下材料避免过度正式，也不故意堆砌年轻人黑话，适合你在法国大学真实使用。
场景一：第一天上课认识同学
Vous：
Salut, cette place est libre ?
你好，这个位置有人吗？
Étudiant：
Oui, vas-y.
没人，你坐吧。
Vous：
Merci. C’est bien le cours du master El Karoui ?
谢谢。这里是El Karoui硕士的课吧？
Étudiant：
Oui. Toi aussi, tu es dans le master ?
对。你也在这个硕士项目吗？
Vous：
Oui, je suis en M2 à Sorbonne Université. Je viens d’arriver en France, donc je découvre encore un peu
tout.
对，我在索邦大学读M2。我刚到法国，所以还在熟悉各种事情。
Étudiant：
Tu viens d’où ?
你来自哪里？
Vous：
Je viens de Chine. J’ai surtout étudié les maths et les probabilités avant de venir ici. Et toi, tu as fait
quelle école ?
我来自中国。来这里以前，我主要学习数学和概率。你呢，你之前读的是哪所学校？
Étudiant：
J’ai fait une école d’ingénieurs à Lyon.
我在里昂读的工程师学校。

Vous：
D’accord. Tu connaissais déjà beaucoup de monde dans le master ?
好的。你之前已经认识很多项目里的同学了吗？
Étudiant：
Non, pas vraiment. Je connais seulement deux personnes.
没有，也不算认识很多。我只认识两个人。
Vous：
Ça me rassure, je ne connais encore personne.
那我放心了，我现在还谁都不认识。
初识高频句型
• Cette place est libre ?
这个位置有人吗？
• Je peux m’asseoir ici ?
我可以坐这里吗？
• Tu es aussi dans ce master ?
你也在这个硕士吗？
• Tu as fait quoi avant ?
你之前是做什么／学什么的？非常口语。
• Tu as fait quelle école ?
你之前读的哪个学校？
• Tu viens d’où ?
你来自哪里？
• Tu habites où ?
你住在哪里？
• Tu connais déjà du monde ici ?
你已经认识这里的一些人了吗？
du monde 在这里表示“人、一些人”：
Il y a beaucoup de monde.
人很多。
Je connais du monde dans cette école.
我在这个学校认识一些人。

场景二：介绍自己的住所
Étudiant：
Tu habites dans Paris ?
你住在巴黎市区吗？
Vous：
Non, j’habite à Vitry-sur-Seine, dans le 94.
不，我住在Vitry-sur-Seine，在94省。
Étudiant：
Ce n’est pas trop loin ?
会不会太远？
Vous：
Ça dépend du campus et des transports, mais ça va. J’habite au [numéro], [nom de la rue].
取决于校区和交通，不过还可以。我住在［街道名称］［门牌号］。
Étudiant：
Tu es en appartement ?
你住公寓吗？
Vous：
Non, c’est une petite maison de plain-pied divisée en deux studios. On est deux à y habiter et chacun a
son propre studio.
不是，是一栋分成两个studio的单层小房子。一共住两个人，每个人都有自己的studio。
Étudiant：
Ça a l’air sympa.
听起来挺不错的。
Vous：
Oui, c’est plutôt calme. Il y a même un petit jardin avec deux arbres fruitiers.
对，比较安静。甚至还有一个小院子，里面有两棵果树。
描述居住体验
• C’est plutôt calme.
比较安静。

• Le quartier est agréable.
这个街区挺舒服。
• C’est bien desservi.
公共交通比较方便。
• Le trajet est un peu long.
通勤有点长。
• Je mets environ quarante minutes pour venir.
我来这里大约要40分钟。
• Je dois prendre le bus puis le métro.
我需要先坐公交再坐地铁。
• Je suis encore en train de m’habituer au trajet.
我还在适应通勤路线。
• Le logement est petit, mais ça me suffit.
房子不大，但够我用了。
Ça me suffit ：对我来说够了。
场景三：说明自己的法语水平并切换英语
Étudiant：
Tu parles français depuis longtemps ?
你学法语很久了吗？
Vous：
Pas du tout. J’ai commencé récemment. Je peux gérer quelques situations simples, mais je ne suis pas
encore capable d’avoir une conversation compliquée.
完全没有。我最近才开始。我可以处理一些简单场景，但还不能进行复杂对话。
Étudiant：
Franchement, tu te débrouilles déjà bien.
说真的，你已经说得不错了。
Vous：
Merci, mais je prépare souvent mes phrases à l’avance. Pour les sujets techniques, je comprends
beaucoup mieux en anglais.
谢谢，但我很多句子都是提前准备的。对于技术话题，我用英语理解得好得多。

Étudiant：
On peut parler anglais si tu préfères.
你更愿意的话，我们可以说英语。
Vous：
Oui, ce serait plus simple pour moi. Mais n’hésite pas à me parler un peu en français aussi. J’ai besoin
de pratiquer.
好，那对我来说会简单一些。不过你也可以和我说一点法语，我需要练习。
语言交流高频句型
Je débute en français.
我刚开始学法语。
Je comprends mieux que je ne parle.
我的理解能力比表达能力好。
Je comprends l’idée générale, mais je rate parfois les détails.
我能理解大意，但有时会漏掉细节。
Je connais le mot en anglais, mais pas en français.
我知道这个词的英语，但不知道法语。
Comment on dit [英文词] en français ?
……用法语怎么说？
同学之间自然说 Comment on dit... ；正式语法也可以说：
Comment dit-on... ?
Ça veut dire quoi ?
这是什么意思？非常口语。
稍微完整：
Qu’est-ce que ça veut dire ?
Tu peux répéter un peu plus lentement ?
你可以慢一点重复吗？

Désolé, je n’ai pas capté la dernière phrase.
不好意思，我没听懂最后一句。
capter 在年轻人口语中常表示“听懂、理解”：
Je n’ai pas capté.
我没听懂。
初学阶段自己可以优先说：
Je n’ai pas compris.
场景四：讨论课程和考试
Vous：
Tu sais si les gens vont vraiment à tous les cours ?

Étudiant：
Ça dépend des matières. Pour certains cours, les gens travaillent surtout avec les polys et les annales.
取决于科目。有些课程大家主要靠讲义和往年试题学习。
Vous：
D’accord. Tu sais où on peut trouver les annales ?
好的。你知道在哪里可以找到往年试题吗？
Étudiant：
Normalement, les étudiants de l’année dernière ont partagé un dossier.

Tu pourrais m’envoyer le lien quand tu l’auras ?

Merci. Et pour cet examen, tu sais si on a le droit d’utiliser une calculatrice ?

Je ne suis pas sûr. Il faudra demander au prof.

最有效的同学聊天结构
不要只回答一个词。使用：
回答问题＋补充一条信息＋反问对方
例如：
Question：
Tu habites où ?
过短：
À Vitry.
自然回答：
J’habite à Vitry-sur-Seine, dans le 94. Le trajet est un peu long, mais le quartier est assez calme. Et toi, tu
habites dans Paris ?
Question：
Tu vises quel type de poste ?
自然回答：
Je m’intéresse surtout à la recherche quantitative, mais je garde l’esprit ouvert. Pour l’instant, je
prépare surtout les probabilités et les algorithmes. Et toi, tu vises plutôt la recherche ou le trading ?
Question：
Tu parles français depuis longtemps ?
自然回答：
Non, j’ai commencé récemment. Je comprends quelques phrases simples, mais je suis beaucoup plus à
l’aise en anglais. Tu as déjà rencontré beaucoup d’étudiants internationaux dans le programme ?
这种“回答＋补充＋反问”是让对话继续下去的核心技巧。
